social_history.living_situation: Lives alone; daughter checks in daily

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait disorder and cognitive decline attributed to 'back issues' — admitted for NPH evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: A 67-year-old right-handed woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and lumbar spinal stenosis was admitted for NPH evaluation after her outpatient neurologist identified ventriculomegaly on brain MRI obtained to evaluate cognitive concerns. The patient has had a progressive gait disorder over 12 months which she and her family attributed entirely to her known lumbar spinal stenosis. However, her spine surgeon noted that her gait pattern does not match typical lumbar stenosis neurogenic claudication (which typically worsens with standing/walking and improves with sitting/flexion — no such positional pattern is present). She has significant memory difficulties over the same period (HbA1c 8.4% — poorly controlled diabetes is a contributing factor per her endocrinologist). She has urinary incontinence on top of pre-existing urge incontinence from diabetes-related bladder dysfunction. MRI brain shows Evans index 0.30 (borderline) with callosal angle 91 degrees (just above 90 degree threshold — does not meet NPH criterion). MRI lumbar spine shows multilevel stenosis. The competing diagnoses (lumbar stenosis for gait, diabetes for cognition) make this a moderate-difficulty case.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3. MoCA 21/30. Losses on attention, delayed recall, and executive function.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal upper extremity strength. Mild proximal lower extremity weakness 4+/5 bilaterally (could be diabetic amyotrophy vs lumbar stenosis). Lower extremity tone mildly increased.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced vibration and light touch bilateral feet (diabetic peripheral neuropathy pattern). Mild saddle anesthesia — lumbar stenosis component.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Patellar diminished bilaterally (2- vs 1+). Achilles absent bilaterally (diabetes/neuropathy). Plantar flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Short-stepped, wide-based, shuffling. Does NOT worsen with prolonged walking or improve with sitting forward (unlike lumbar stenosis neurogenic claudication). TUG 30 seconds. 10-meter walk 24 seconds.
neurological_exam.additional: No clonus. No upper motor neuron signs. Lumbar range of motion limited. Obesity complicates gait assessment.

mri.impression: 1. Brain MRI: Ventriculomegaly; Evans index 0.30. Callosal angle 91 degrees on coronal imaging. Moderate bilateral periventricular and subcortical white matter hyperintensity. 2. Lumbar MRI: Severe bilateral lateral recess stenosis at L3-4 and L4-5. Clinical correlation recommended.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Glucose 162 mg/dL (H), HbA1c 8.4 % (H), MMA 320 nmol/L (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 46 mg/dL. Glucose: 68 mg/dL (ratio 0.42). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 644 pg/mL (borderline low; reference >650). total_tau: 258 pg/mL (borderline elevated). phospho_tau: 48 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with gait analysis

findings.note: Gait quality post-tap: step height improved, less wide-based; lower extremity weakness persists (lumbar/diabetes component unchanged)

specialized_test.impression: High-volume tap trial (40 mL): TUG improved from 30 seconds pre-tap to 24 seconds at 24 hours (20% improvement). 10-meter walk improved from 24 to 19.5 seconds (19% improvement). MoCA improved 1 point at 24 hours. Post-tap gait: step height improved, less wide-based; lower extremity weakness component unchanged. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Extended lumbar drainage (72 hours): progressive gait improvement — TUG from 30 seconds baseline to 21 seconds at day 3 (30% improvement). Clinical correlation recommended.

Phase-contrast MRI (aqueductal CSF flow): peak velocity 19 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); net stroke volume 55 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Mildly hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF pulsatility identified. Clinical correlation recommended.
Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 20, below the amyloid positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Impaired lower extremity — neuropathy and lumbar stenosis

quantitative_data.pattern: Multiple contributing factors: NPH frontal-subcortical + diabetic cognitive impairment + functional B12 deficiency

output.impression: Neuropsychological evaluation demonstrates severely impaired processing speed, moderately impaired executive function, mildly impaired episodic memory, and impaired sensory-motor function in lower extremities. Multiple contributors to cognitive and motor impairment are identified. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Concurrent diabetic bladder dysfunction — reduced bladder sensation

output.impression: Mixed urinary dysfunction: neurogenic detrusor overactivity with involuntary contractions and concurrent reduced bladder sensation pattern. No outlet obstruction. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: B12 supplementation 1000 mcg IM + continue metformin
interactions: Metformin reduces ileal B12 absorption — parenteral B12 bypasses this mechanism; continue metformin for diabetes management
warnings: Monitor B12 levels annually given ongoing metformin use
Oral B12 supplementation may be less effective given metformin-induced malabsorption — IM preferred initially
alternatives: High-dose oral B12 (1000-2000 mcg/day) as alternative if IM not tolerated

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Occasional premature atrial complexes, a benign finding. No acute ST-T changes.
ecg.interpretation: Largely normal ECG with a benign incidental finding

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

cardiac_monitoring.rhythm_summary: Predominant sinus rhythm throughout the recording
findings: Brief runs of asymptomatic sinus tachycardia. No sustained arrhythmia, no pauses greater than 2 seconds, no AV block.
cardiac_monitoring.impression: 24-hour Holter monitor with only benign findings.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

differential.key_features: MRI shows severe multilevel stenosis — but gait does not show neurogenic claudication pattern (no improvement with sitting/flexion); gait improvement post-tap argues for NPH component
HbA1c 8.4%, poorly controlled — may contribute to cognition but does not explain ventriculomegaly or gait disorder
Low-normal B12, elevated MMA from metformin — contributing to neuropathy; B12 replacement warranted but does not fully explain the syndrome
Moderate WMH, hypertension, diabetes — but Evans 0.30, positive drainage trial support NPH as primary diagnosis

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Evans 0.30 (borderline), callosal angle 91, moderate WMH; severe lumbar stenosis

optimal_actions.action: Comprehensive labs including HbA1c, B12, MMA
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Poor diabetes control, functional B12 deficiency from metformin

optimal_actions.action: High-volume tap trial despite borderline imaging
B12 IM supplementation for functional deficiency
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Treat reversible contributor to neuropathy and cognition

optimal_actions.action: Extended drainage trial for equivocal tap
VP shunt after confirmed extended drainage response

critical_actions: B12/MMA testing critical — metformin-induced functional B12 deficiency is a treatable contributor
Tap trial still indicated despite borderline imaging (Evans 0.30 exactly at threshold)
Gait does not follow neurogenic claudication pattern despite severe lumbar stenosis — NPH triad persists
Do not attribute all symptoms to lumbar stenosis or diabetes without tap trial
contraindicated_actions: Attributing gait disorder entirely to lumbar stenosis without brain MRI and tap trial
Withholding NPH evaluation because imaging is borderline
Starting high-dose anticholinergics for bladder symptoms without considering cognitive risk
key_reasoning_points: Multiple competing diagnoses make this moderate difficulty: lumbar stenosis (gait), diabetes (cognition and neuropathy), B12 deficiency (neuropathy), vascular (WMH) — and NPH on top
Functional B12 deficiency from metformin (elevated MMA with low-normal B12) is an important reversible finding
Gait pattern does not match neurogenic claudication (positional) — magnetic gait suggests NPH despite lumbar pathology
Extended drainage trial overcomes borderline tap trial result and borderline imaging
Multiple simultaneous treatments needed: B12 replacement, diabetes optimization, and VP shunt for NPH

red_herrings.data_point: Severe multilevel lumbar stenosis on spine MRI
red_herrings.intended_effect: Gait disorder attributed entirely to lumbar spinal stenosis — NPH evaluation deferred
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Gait does not follow neurogenic claudication pattern; tap trial response confirms NPH as contributor; both lumbar stenosis and NPH coexist

red_herrings.intended_effect: Cognitive decline attributed to poorly controlled diabetes rather than NPH
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Poorly controlled diabetes contributes to cognition but does not explain ventriculomegaly or gait disorder; NPH evaluation warranted regardless

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Moderate NPH with multiple competing diagnoses: severe lumbar stenosis, poorly controlled diabetes, functional B12 deficiency (metformin), and vascular white matter disease — borderline imaging (Evans exactly 0.30, callosal angle 91).
